description:
SGP is seeking an experienced Proposal Manager to support a dedicated, ongoing engagement with a tribally owned 8(a) small business specializing in secure, mission-critical solutions for federal customers. You will lead proposal efforts across a diverse portfolio, including secure construction and design-build, facility support and security, cyber and IT modernization, infrastructure and power, healthcare and health IT, procurement and logistics, and professional services, supporting defense and civilian agencies.

You’ll bring experience working successfully in a 1099 capacity and be comfortable integrating closely with client leadership, business development, and technical teams while coordinating with SGP's broader consultant network. You‘ll also have a demonstrated ability to partner with capture managers and coordinators, proposal coordinators, writers, editors, graphic designers, and pricing and contracts professionals to deliver cohesive, competitive proposals.

Workplace Type: Remote.

Compensation: 1099 Consultant. $100 - $120 per hour.

Security Clearance: Active Security Clearance.

Why Join the SGP Capture & Proposals Team

As an SGP consultant, you'll enjoy the independence and flexibility of 1099 work while benefiting from the resources, collaboration, and professional support of an experienced capture and proposals team.

  • Select consultant network: Join a network of experienced capture and proposal professionals who bring diverse expertise and collaborate to support client needs across a variety of engagements.

  • The right fit, by design: We strive to align each consultant with client engagements that complement their professional expertise, career interests, and working styles, creating opportunities for meaningful contributions and successful collaboration.

  • Referral bonuses: Earn referral incentives for introducing prospective clients and qualified consultants to the SGP network, subject to program eligibility requirements.

  • Resources that raise the bar: Access optional professional development opportunities, established templates, industry best practices, and support from experienced professionals to strengthen the quality and efficiency of your work.

  • Flexibility and choice: Enjoy the flexibility of remote consulting and the opportunity to accept engagements that align with your availability, expertise, and professional interests.

  • Modern, AI-enabled workflows: Collaborate with a team that combines extensive federal contracting expertise with modern technologies and evolving AI-assisted tools and processes to support efficient, high-quality proposal development.

  • Breadth of experience: Gain exposure to a variety of federal agencies, contract vehicles, and clients, ranging from emerging small businesses to established government contractors.

Responsibilities

  • Lead proposals from kickoff through submission across construction, security, technology, products, and professional services requirements.

  • Manage 8(a) sole-source and direct-award responses, including technical and cost proposals prepared for contracting officer review and negotiation.

  • Manage design-build and construction proposals, including two-phase design-build, JOC and MATOC task orders, and secure facility requirements, such as SCIFs designed to meet ICD 705 standards.

  • Manage services proposals, including staffing plans, key personnel, transition approaches, and management volumes.

  • Analyze solicitations and develop compliance matrices, annotated outlines, schedules, and storyboards.

  • Run kickoff meetings, status calls, and color team reviews.

  • Collaborate with SMEs, estimators, and engineers to develop technical approaches, and coordinate with pricing teams on cost volumes and basis-of-estimate narratives.

  • Develop past performance write-ups highlighting experience in secure, highly sensitive environments.

  • Integrate capture strategies, win themes, and discriminators into compelling, compliant proposal content.

  • Oversee final production, quality checks, and timely submission.

Required qualifications

  • At least five years of experience in federal proposal management.

  • Demonstrated experience managing proposals in at least two of the following areas: federal construction and design-build; facility support and physical or electronic security; cybersecurity and IT modernization; infrastructure, telecommunications, and power; health IT; or professional services.

  • Experience developing 8(a) proposals, including sole-source and set-aside responses.

  • Experience supporting the Department of Defense (DoD) and federal civilian customers.

  • Strong command of Shipley or equivalent proposal management best practices.

  • Excellent organizational, writing, and editing skills with the ability to meet tight deadlines.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience supporting tribally owned or Alaska Native Corporation 8(a) firms.

  • Experience developing task order responses under JOC, MATOC, SATOC, and other construction and facilities IDIQ contracts.

  • Experience developing joint venture proposals.

  • Familiarity with construction estimating and basis-of-estimate development.

  • · APMP Foundation-level, Practitioner, or Professional certification.

  • Active security clearance.
